doc_name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim – Dragonborn
text: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim – Dragonborn is the third and final expansion for the action role-playing open world game The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, developed by Bethesda Game Studios and released by Bethesda Softworks on the Xbox Live Marketplace on December 4, 2012. The Microsoft Windows version launched on February 5, 2013, and the PlayStation 3 version was released on February 12, 2013 in North America and February 13, 2013 in Europe. The expansion takes place on the island of Solstheim, previously featured in the Bloodmoon expansion for The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, which was once part of Skyrim and given to Morrowind as a refuge for Dunmer fleeing after the Red Mountain volcano eruption. Half of Solstheim resembles northern Skyrim with icy glaciers and snow, while the other half is barren and ash-covered. The island features Nordic architecture in the northern region and Dunmeri-style buildings, including a house formed from a giant mushroom, with the main settlement, Raven Rock, governed by House Redoran and protected by the Redoran Guard. The main quest begins when the player, the Last Dragonborn, is attacked by cultists worshipping Miraak, the First Dragonborn. Investigating the cultists reveals their connection to Solstheim, leading the player to charter the ship Northern Maiden from Windhelm to Raven Rock. Upon arrival, the player interrogates locals and discovers that most of Solstheim’s population is unconsciously enslaved by Miraak, who forces them to work on All-Maker Stones. A Telvanni wizard, Neloth, guides the player to the Temple of Miraak, where they encounter Frea, a Nord immune to Miraak’s control, who attempts to break the spell over the Skaal. Inside, the player finds a Black Book and is transported to Apocrypha, a realm of Oblivion, where they witness Miraak planning to invade Tamriel. Miraak captures the player, dismisses them as inferior, and sends Seekers to return them to Solstheim. Upon return, the player visits Skaal Village, where shaman Storn instructs them to perform a special dragon shout on an All-Maker Stone, purifying it and freeing the Skaal and others from Miraak’s control, while fighting Lurkers sent to reclaim the stones. Neloth reveals the Black Books are relics of Hermaeus Mora, the Daedric Prince of Fate, Knowledge, and Memory, the source of Miraak’s power. The player and Neloth travel to the Dwemer ruin of Nchardak to retrieve another Black Book, where they learn of the shout "Bend Will," believed to defeat Miraak. After returning to Apocrypha, the player encounters Hermaeus Mora, who offers knowledge in exchange for the Skaal’s secrets. Despite Frea’s protests, Storn surrenders the secrets, and Mora drains him of knowledge, killing him in front of the village. The player then learns the final word of "Bend Will," enabling them to defeat Miraak. The player returns to Apocrypha, uses "Bend Will" to subdue Miraak’s dragon Sahrotaar, mounts it, and flies to Miraak’s tower, the Summit of Apocrypha. There, Miraak sacrifices his dragons Relonikiv and Kruziikrel and Sahrotaar to regain strength, but Hermaeus Mora intervenes, fatally impaling Miraak and expressing anger at his rebellion and betrayal. Mora transfers Miraak’s soul and power to the player, who is then returned to Solstheim. The Summit of Apocrypha becomes a location where the player can exchange dragon souls for perk points to customize skills. The soundtrack includes music from The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind and new tracks composed by Jeremy Soule, who has composed soundtracks for several games in the series. Dragonborn was originally announced via a trailer on November 5, 2012. The expansion received mainly positive critical reception, with GamesRadar praising the side quests, new weapons, and dragon shouts, though dismissing the dragon riding feature as "gimmicky." Eurogamer gave the content 9 out of 10, praising the quests, new enemies, and new locations. Joystiq commended the amount of content, including new settings and enemies, but felt the narrative was too familiar.
